name: Shikla
summary: A shikla or shakila (Arabic: شكيلة), also known under the name alama (علامة) is a piece of clothing that the Jews of Tunisia were forced to wear to distinguish themselves from Muslim residents.
description: A shikla or shakila (Arabic: شكيلة), also known under the name alama (علامة) is a piece of clothing that the Jews of Tunisia were forced to wear to distinguish themselves from Muslim residents. The shikla was primarily worn, with some interruptions, between the 9th and 19th century in Tunisia and at times also in the rest of the Maghreb.

visualDNA.Overview: The requirements for the shikla varied with the different dynasties that ruled over Tunisia. The main goal was simply to distinguish and humiliate Jews in public spaces. Under the reign of the Almohad Caliphate, it was principally a turban dyed yellow at the end. Jewish converts to Islam were forced to wear a long dark blue tunic with sleeves so large they reached one's feet, and a skullcap in place of a turban. During the mid-fifteenth century the shikla consisted of a piece of yellow fabric.
